newsitem.title: USA: Jury awards $223 million in Dow Jones libel suit.
newsitem.headline: Jury awards $223 million in Dow Jones libel suit.

text.p: A federal jury Thursday awarded a defunct securities firm $222.7 million in damages in a libel suit against Dow Jones & Co. Inc., the publisher of the Wall Street Journal.
Plaintiffs' attorneys said it was the biggest jury award ever in a libel case.

The jury's decision followed a two-week trial in which Houston-based MMAR Group Inc. said it had been forced out of business by a critical, error-filled article published in the Wall Street Journal on Oct. 21, 1993.

The article, by reporter Laura Jereski, said that a Louisiana pension fund had lost money because of MMAR's mishandling of complex financial instruments known as derivatives and that MMAR was facing legal action. Witnesses for the plaintiffs contended that both points were wrong and the jury of two men and five women agreed.

The award included $22.7 million for the value of the company and $200 million in punitive damages. Corey Minor, one of the principals of MMAR, gasped and wept audibly in the cavernous courtroom when the verdict was read.
Dow Jones attorney David Donaldson defended the story and said the decision would be appealed.
He said Jereski had talked to more than 30 sources, including former employees of the company and National Association of Securities Dealers investigators, before the article was published.

MMAR attorney Mark Harwell accused of Jereski of setting out to do a "hatchet job" on the company and said Journal editors had not given her enough direction. MMAR's revenues dropped by 52 percent after the article came out and the company had to close its doors a month later, he said.
"She was the judge, jury and executioner of MMAR," he said of Jereski.
Harwell said the previous biggest jury award in a libel case was $57 million against a Waco, Texas television station.
"This case will send a message to Dow Jones," he said. "It's hard to rebuild a reputation."
Donaldson said the verdict proved again that large media companies are "at a disadvantage" in libel cases.
A spokesman for Dow Jones was not immediately available for comment.
